newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed, blue chips still soft.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed, blue chips still soft.

text.p: Buyers continued to focus on the small-capitalisation counters, boosting the Second Board index deeper into record territory after a quiet session.
The Composite Index, a blue chip barometer, ended down 2.12 points to 1,111.33. The Second Board index added 4.63 points or 0.86 percent to 541.75, its third closing high in a row.

"The Second Board is running up like nobody's business," remarked a dealer with a bank-linked brokerage firm, adding that 550 on the Second Board index is seen as a resistance level. Heavy retail buying and speculative interest has been driving up the sector.
Blue chips stayed on lower ground just about all day even as secondary issues leapt to fresh records. The Second Board index touched a high of 543.02 during the day before giving up some gains.

Local investors and overseas syndicates were probably behind the Second Board's meteoric rise, dealers said. "It's pure speculation," a dealer said. "Blue chips have to depend on economic fundamentals."
By day's end, more than 223 million shares had changed hands, with the Second Board almost matching the main board in turnover. Losers outpaced gainers by 311 to 235.
